findings.title: II Samuel 8:3: the written half's own card is now gated under read word 1's entry
findings.where: reader/zone.html tagHolder/tagsAt (about lines 3300-3306); the place is II Samuel 8:3, word 12 (section 189, entry 11)
findings.evidence: The written half (בנהר) and read word 1 בִּֽנְהַר have the same key, בנהר. tagsAt matches by key, so after the apply the written form's own card picks up read word 1's tag. Page probe on shipped main + this commit + applied zones: «form (בנהר) ketiv — written · __cardEntry "H5104G" · readings ask "H5104G", withhold 2 · 2 of another entry than H5104G, withheld». The two rows withheld are TAHOT M4 ranks 2 and 3, «at/ [the] river of» and «in the/ river», both lettered H5104H. On the shipped zones no region at this place carries a tag, so the written card asked no entry before. The page's own comment above tagHolder says the written half of a pair takes none, and E12 says a form its place gives no tag is not gated. I scanned every listed place: this is the only one where a written half shares its key with a read word. No check sees it. R7 reads only the read words' blocks, E6 and E7 never run tagsAt, and the commit message says only the read words' blocks change. The function-level diff shows the cause is the tagged data plus key matching. On the applied zones the old tagsAt also returns [H5104G] for בנהר; on the shipped zones it returns null.

findings.title: E7's check without the lattice accepts any tag on a written half beside tagged read words
findings.where: reader/tools/check-entry-gate-v1.mjs, E7 (the own/halves split in the zone walk)
findings.evidence: In a scratch copy of job.bin I tagged the written half at Job 38:1 with H4480A beside its two tagged read words and raised the receipt's places_tagged by 1. The new E7 without --lattice passes (exit 0). With --lattice, its second half fails: «job 38:1 word 5: carries H4480A on מנהסערה; the lattice's core tags are none». check-read-words-v1 does not see it, because R3 reads only the read words. The relaxation is needed for the four places where the lattice itself tags the written half (Deuteronomy 33:2, Jeremiah 6:29, Psalms 55:16, I Chronicles 9:4). At all four, the written half's tags equal the read words' main tags in order. Before the ship, a receipt-consistent forged tag on a lone written half also passed the first half, so no refusal is lost. But on a machine without the lattice, such as CI, nothing judges it. A well-formed but wrong read-word tag (Job 38:12 read word 1 given H3046) also passes E7, by design; R3 and R7 caught it.

outcomes.evidence:
Reproduced:
- The line at rest reads «common + broken», credited M9 M14, both before and after the ship.
- On the read form's card after the ship, block חל asks H2428A, withholds 50 of 60, and opens on «surrounding». Block כאים asks H3512B, withholds 1 (M3 «helpless»), and opens on «broken».
- Before the ship (shipped page, shipped zones), both blocks asked nothing, and חל opened on «common».
- Every row printing «common» carries n H2455 and is called «other» under H2428A: M17, M9 and M14 «common», M5 «commonness», M46 «profaneness | commonness». The 10 rows kept carry no facts.

Why it is left for the lead: plan 4.2 rules this exact state («Psalms 10:10's tags land, but its pieces are held until put-back 35»; 19 lines with Psalms 10:10 held). Every remedy changes ruled figures. Measured options:
- (a) Hold both tags. 54 tags land; withheld 1,022 (1,073 − 50 − 1), own 1,563 − 4 = 1,559. The pin entry must hold tags too, and the apply's dry-run line, R3, R5 and ship2-steps.sh change from 56 to 54.
- (b) Ship as planned and note it for the owner.
- (c) Hold only read word 1's tag H2428A. 55 tags; withheld 1,023, own 1,563. Read word 2's line «broken» is of its own entry, so it does not disagree.
